title: Market Selloff Deepens as Investors Seek Shelter
text:
Market Selloff Deepens as Investors Seek Shelter
JJ Kinahan is Senior Vice President, Head of Retail Expansion and Alternative Investment Products at Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe).
S&P 500 and Dow officially in correction territory
There is a lot to say about what happened in Friday’s tumultuous trading session, but probably the most relevant is that it’s over, marking the end of an eventful week.
As I noted after Thursday’s pressure-cooker of a session, Friday might be more telling of whether we’re watching the final stage of November’s selloff or whether investors would step in to buy the dip while navigating an unusually wide range of volatility.
It didn’t appear that a lot of folks moved in to a market that looked to be steered by investor angst amid the wall of worry taking shape. The Cboe Volatility Index ® (the VIX ® Index) climbed nearly 26%, flirting with 36, its highest level since the tariff-driven market mayhem of April 2025. Friday’s sharp upturn likely reflected an escape to protection rather than an immediate buying opportunity.
When the bell rang, the milestones were cemented: the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were officially in correction zones with the S&P 500 breaking below 7,000. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3%, wiping out an entire year of advances that even the biggest initial public offering (IPO) ever could not contain. The Nasdaq 100 Index was dangerously close to bear market territory, which is a decline of 20% or more.
Anthropic’s extraordinary debut in the market Thursday is history now with the parent of Claude losing more than 9% It seems the company got caught up the same way the rest of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector has. Nvidia was another big loser, giving back nearly 14% on reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating the chipmaker’s accounting practices. Since the scandal surrounding former Chief Executive Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and other issues surfaced Nov. 8, Nvidia has erased a stunning $1.4 trillion in market capitalization.
The silver lining, if you can call it that, was in Treasurys. The 10-year Treasury rate fell below 5% as investors appeared to seek shelter in government debt over stocks.
Bull markets never move in straight lines and corrections historically pop up about every 18 months. But Friday’s cap to a series of tough selloffs raises a bigger question: Is this simply a reset or, as I noted Thursday, are investors grappling with a broader set of risks? Higher interest rates are still on the table, conflicts in the Middle East are not resolved and there is still little insight into what might be behind the string of technology and power outages over the past week.
Market commentators tossed around suggestions Friday that the AI pullbacks and broader market selloff were oversold. That may be true and some investors might consider the rout a washout that creates buying opportunities at more attractive prices.
But a rebound next week wouldn’t necessarily mean the correction is over. It could simply represent a reset in tech stocks and the broader market. In any case, investors would be wise to proceed with caution.
